newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: EU backs continued ACP nations trade support.
newsitem.headline: EU backs continued ACP nations trade support.

text.p: The European Union remains committed to supportive trade ties with developing African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) nations despite a global push for free markets, an EU official said on Tuesday.

Speaking in an interview at the International Sugar Organisation meeting in Mauritius, he said the EU was a strong supporter of the Lome Sugar Protocol, an agreement giving ACP countries preferential access to the markets of the continent.

"Although we recognise that we will have to open our markets more and move our support payments from production support to direct payments to farmers, we are not about to dismantle our common agricultural policy," said the official who asked not to be identified.
"There is no widespread support for that."
The comments follow ACP-member and sugar-dependant Mauritius's criticism on Monday of world pressures for trade liberalisation raised at the recent Uruguay GATT trade talks.

The Indian Ocean island, which under the sugar protocol exports almost its entire crop to Europe each year making this its biggest foreign exchange earner by far, said an end to the trade protection could cripple its economy.
"Our position and Mauritius's position would be very similar on (the sugar protocol)," said the official.
"There are other factors other than unrestrained free trade when you look at agriculture. There are social factors and economic factors to ensure that your farmers earn a decent living."
The official said that future renegotiations of Lome would depend largely on the opinions on free trade expressed in the World Trade Organisation, the successor to GATT.
Discussions leading up to a new trade agreement were expected to be intense and complex, forming part of a wider political debate about aid and how it should be administered, he said.

"But I am quite sure that the EU will want to continue to be encouraging the economic development of those countries within the Lome area and in relation to sugar to those countries to which sugar is an important crop."
